transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we have the battery-storage installation for the distribution campus on this month's capital-planning agenda. The current proposal is a $6 million purchase with company ownership. Before I make an approval decision, I'd like to hear from each of you — FP&A, tax, treasury, and legal — on anything relevant to this project. Please go ahead.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed the project cash-flow model this morning. At the company's required return hurdle, the economically approvable purchase price is exactly $4,800,000 — the $6,000,000 proposal does not pass the model's hurdle. I have not yet attached the completed model to the investment-review file, but I'm sharing this now so Maya has it before making a decision.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag an important tax consideration. I received a tax memorandum this week confirming that the 30% investment credit for this battery-storage installation is available only when the company owns the equipment. If we were to structure this as a lease instead of a purchase, that credit would be unavailable. I had not yet circulated the memorandum to the planning team, but given that ownership structure is relevant to the approval decision, I'm sharing it now.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: From a treasury perspective, I need to flag a funding constraint. In today's rolling cash forecast, I confirmed that only $2,000,000 can be deployed without breaching our operating-liquidity floor. The remaining $2,800,000 can be funded through an available five-year term-loan facility. I have not yet updated the funding worksheet, but given that this project is on the agenda for a decision, I want to make sure Maya has this information before approving.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: From a legal perspective, I need to flag two conditions I found in the utility interconnection agreement this week. Energization of the battery-storage system requires a $400,000 performance bond and a signed commissioning certificate before the system can be placed in service. I have not yet added these conditions to the draft approval, but given that we're making a decision today, Maya should be aware that these are prerequisites before the system can go live — and the performance bond represents an additional cost commitment on top of the $6,000,000 purchase price.
